maps.title: Physics Research Workflow
maps.description: Pre-run and iterative workflow for physics research with baseline gates, validation, researcher review, and lineage.

nodes.title: 1. Intake
nodes.summary: Decide whether this is a new project or an existing research retrofit.
checks: Do not reorganize old artifacts before inventory.
Mark existing validation status honestly.

nodes.title: 2. Orient Gate
nodes.summary: Record task classification, responsible role, first professor question, and suggested next skill before research work begins.
checks: The run has an orient note before Seed, Execute, or Evaluate work starts.
The first researcher-facing question is explicit.

nodes.title: 3. Interview Gate
nodes.summary: Freeze the crystallized research question, surfaced assumptions, agreed direction, and next skill before seed design or execution.
checks: Research object, observable, and review checkpoint are not ambiguous.
Execution remains blocked until the interview note records the agreed direction.

nodes.title: 4. Literature Gate
nodes.summary: Decide whether literature review is ready or explicitly waived, including prior methods and the smallest reproduction target when novelty or fidelity matters.
checks: Prior-work, metric, or reproduction choices are recorded before model specification relies on them.
A waiver lowers the claim ceiling and keeps unsupported novelty claims unverified.

nodes.title: 5. Specify Model
nodes.summary: Make physical system, degrees of freedom, equations, parameters, and validity regime explicit.
checks: Variables and parameters are defined.
Initial and boundary conditions are not silent.

nodes.title: 6. Check Dimensions
nodes.summary: Check units, dimensions, constants set to one, and nondimensionalization.
checks: Do not patch missing dimensions by guessing.
Record ambiguous nondimensionalization.

nodes.title: 7. Baseline Gate
nodes.summary: Validate a toy model, known limit, reproduction target, conservation case, or dimensional sanity case.
checks: Do not proceed to full-scale interpretation without pass or explicit waiver.
Record what this baseline does not justify.

nodes.title: 8. Execute Small Iteration
nodes.summary: Run or derive the smallest meaningful result before expanding scope.
checks: Record commands, parameters, seeds, and outputs.
Run smallest relevant validation first.

nodes.title: 9. Anomaly Branch
nodes.summary: If behavior is surprising, classify and reproduce the anomaly before patching.
checks: State expected behavior and observed behavior.
Classify physical, model, numerical, implementation, data, plotting, or unknown.

nodes.title: 10. Researcher Review
nodes.summary: Package results for researcher judgment and record decisions.
checks: Separate observations, interpretation, and speculation.
State what the researcher needs to confirm.

nodes.title: 11. Claim Gate
nodes.summary: Before strengthening a claim, map evidence and choose safe wording.
checks: Use the weakest wording supported by evidence.
Do not infer mechanism or universality without support.

nodes.title: 12. Retrospective
nodes.summary: Record what changed, evidence delta, reusable artifact, and next smallest iteration.
checks: Every iteration should leave a reusable artifact or explain why not.
Update research state for the next session.

nodes.title: Paper Path?
nodes.summary: If the result may become a paper, move into the paper logic map before drafting strong claims.
checks: Do not draft manuscript logic stronger than the evidence chain.
Map each result to a claim role.

maps.title: Paper Logic Structure
maps.description: Logical path from research question to manuscript claims, including evidence gates and limitation handling.

nodes.title: 1. Research Question
nodes.summary: State the precise physical question the paper can answer.
checks: Question is answerable by the model and data.

nodes.title: 2. Literature Gap
nodes.summary: State what is missing in prior work without inventing novelty.
checks: Novelty claims need citation support.

nodes.title: 3. Model and Assumptions
nodes.summary: Introduce the model only as far as needed to support the paper question.
checks: Assumptions and validity regime are visible.

nodes.title: 4. Methods and Validation
nodes.summary: Show how analytical, numerical, or empirical methods were validated.
checks: Validation is adequate for the intended claim level.

nodes.title: 5. Result
nodes.summary: Present the core result with uncertainty, regime, and provenance.
checks: Result links back to scripts, data, equations, or logs.

nodes.title: 6. Claim
nodes.summary: Translate result into the strongest safe manuscript claim.
checks: Claim language matches evidence level.

nodes.title: 7. Limitations
nodes.summary: State what the model, data, and validation do not justify.
checks: Limitations include failed or partial validation where relevant.

nodes.title: 8. Conclusion
nodes.summary: Return to the research question and state only what is now supported.
checks: Conclusion does not exceed claim gate.
